PAKISTAN POST OFFICE RULES, 1961
PAKISTAN POST OFFICE RULES,
1961
(Amendments)
[Gazette of Pakistan,
Extraordinary, Part II,
14th March, 2011]
S.R.O.228(I)/2011, dated 3-2-2011.---In exercise of
the powers conferred by section 74 of the Post Office Act, 189$ (VI of 1898),
the Federal Government is pleased to direct that the following further
amendments shall be made in the Pakistan Post Office Rules, 1961, namely:
In the aforesaid Rules,--
(a) in rule 105, for the word "ten", the
word "twenty" shall be substituted;
(b) in rule 121, for the word "ten" the
word "twenty" shall be substituted;
(c) in rule 122,
(i) for the words "A commission on the issue of
inland money orders at the flat rate of fifty rupees per money order
irrespective of the value of a single money order up to ten thousand rupees
shall be charged from the remitter" the following shall be substituted,
namely:--
"Value of money order Commission chargeable on a single money order
For a value not exceeding Rs.10,000 Rs.50
For a value exceeding Rs.10,000 and not exceeding Rs.75";
Rs.20,000
(ii) in the first proviso, after the word
"rupees" occurring at the end, the following shall be inserted,
namely:--
"and at the flat rate of fifty rupees for a
single money order above ten thousand rupees but not exceeding twenty thousand
rupees"; and
(d) In rule 155, in sub-rule (1), for the letters,
full stop and figure "Rs.10,000" the words "twenty thousand
rupees" shall be substituted.
